chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, or someone else, from Aban, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When the incisor blackens, the wergild (blood money) is applicable regarding it.'

key_terms.الثَّنِيَّةُ: The incisor tooth (specifically the upper or lower canine/incisor depending on context, often referring to the prominent front teeth in legal contexts of injury)
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: Wergild or blood money, a financial compensation paid for bodily injury or death

ai.seo_question: What is the legal compensation for a blackened incisor tooth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a specific legal precedent in Shia jurisprudence where the blackening of an incisor (thaniyyah) triggers the obligation of diya, reflecting the detailed application of blood money rules in cases of physical injury. It highlights the Imam's role in clarifying the material signs of injury that necessitate compensation, a topic extensively discussed in later works like al-Mahasin and al-Faqih. The ruling underscores the precision with which Shia scholars categorize injuries based on visible changes in the body, such as discoloration, to determine the appropriate financial restitution.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, or someone else, from Aban, from one of his companions, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘When the incisors blacken, the wergild would be applicable regarding it’.
